title: Other VA Benefits Opened by a DIC Award to a Surviving Spouse
content:
Desk guidance for Veterans Service Representatives on the benefits that a Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) award opens for a surviving spouse.

## The rule

Holding DIC opens other benefits: the spouse is eligible for Chapter 35 education benefits, is exempt from the home loan funding fee, and may be eligible for CHAMPVA. DIC is no longer offset against a Survivor Benefit Plan annuity.

## Effect by benefit

| Benefit | Effect of holding DIC | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (Chapter 35) | The spouse is eligible | Eligible |
| VA home loan funding fee | The spouse is exempt | Exempt |
| CHAMPVA health coverage | The spouse may be eligible | Possible eligibility only |
| Survivor Benefit Plan annuity | DIC is not offset against it | No offset |

## Points the rule settles

- The three openings — Chapter 35, the funding fee exemption and possible CHAMPVA eligibility — come from holding DIC.
- Chapter 35 eligibility and the funding fee exemption are stated outright; CHAMPVA is stated only as a possibility ("may be eligible").
- A surviving spouse who also receives a Survivor Benefit Plan annuity has no reduction of DIC on account of that annuity.

## Hypothetical illustration

A surviving spouse holds a DIC award and also receives a Survivor Benefit Plan annuity. The DIC amount is not offset against the annuity; the spouse is eligible for Chapter 35 education benefits, is exempt from the VA home loan funding fee, and may be eligible for CHAMPVA.
